en: The build broke again after your last change.
a_st: 리 누 파 에 피 니로 레 후 메루타카
b_st: 리 누 파 에 피 니로 레 후 메루타카
a_lost: 'the build' is the build root used as an argument ('the thing built'); 'broke again' uses the documented repeat-construction ('repeated the failure'); 'last' = 'previous'.
b_lost: 'build' is the bare build-root as an argument ('the thing built'); 'broke' is rendered as the run-time failure root, per the rule that broken is not a root.

en: Did you push that fix yet?
a_st: 에 우 라 파 카푸타 추
b_st: 에 우 라 파 카푸타 추
a_lost: 'push' rendered as give/pass/send; the destination (shared repository) is unstated. 'yet' is unexpressed, as in the corpus.
b_lost: No version-control 'push': rendered with the generic give/pass/send root, so 'to the remote' is not said. 'Yet' has no word at all.

en: Run the tests before you merge anything.
a_st: 에 와 파 에 토 파 투두카디 히 다카마
b_st: 에 와 파 에 토 파 투두카디 히 다카마
a_lost: 'anything' is the bare thing root (number-neutral); no negative-polarity 'any'.
b_lost: 'Anything' is just the bare thing-root; there is no any/indefinite determiner, so the negative-polarity flavour is gone.

en: If the log is empty, the writer never started.
a_st: 미노 왜 푸소코 해 워코디 토 소 유 페 쿠태타키
b_st: 미노 왜 푸소코 해 워 예 소 유 페 쿠태타키
a_lost: No agent-noun derivation, so 'the writer' is a relative clause 'the thing that writes'; 'never' is the none-determiner on the time root.
b_lost: No agent-derivation suffix, so 'the writer' is the compound write-person and could also be read as 'the written person'. 'Never' is the documented no-time phrase.

en: She said the parser chokes on blank lines.
a_st: 우 티패 파 데코디 토 푸소 피토 호 누코디 워야타카
b_st: 우 데 타푸 푸소 피토 페 누코디 워야타카
a_lost: No root for parse; 'parser' becomes 'the thing that reads text', which loses the structural-analysis sense. 'Chokes' flattened to 'fails'. No gender in the pronoun.
b_lost: No root for 'parser'; rendered as 'read function', which a listener would take as any reading code. 'Chokes' flattens to 'fails'. 'She' is the genderless that-one.

en: It must be reading the old config; nothing else explains it.
a_st: 우 파캐루코디 새루 파 데키 소 토 우 파 헤도카
b_st: 우 파캐루코디 새루 파 데키 소 두루코디 토 우 파 헤도카
a_lost: 'else' is unexpressed (only 'nothing'); 'old' is 'not new'; 'must' is the inferred evidential.
b_lost: 'Else' needs the periphrasis 'no not-same thing'; no progressive aspect, so 'must be reading' is just 'reads, inferred'.

en: I'll rewrite the loop tonight.
a_st: 아 메루 워 파 이 카요 페 메루투카마
b_st: 아 파캐 메루 파 이 카요 페 리투카마
a_lost: 'rewrite' is 'repeat the loop-writing'; the loop root and the again root are the same word, so the line repeats it.
b_lost: 'Rewrite' becomes 'build a new loop' (writing the loop again cannot be said directly, since loop and again are the same root). 'Tonight' is 'this night'.

en: This will crash on the second pass.
a_st: 이 메루 네 페 누투키매
b_st: 이 메루 네 페 누투키매
a_lost: 'pass' is the repeat/iteration root; 'crash' is the run-time failure root.
b_lost: 'Pass' is the repeat/iteration root; 'crash' is the failure root.

en: I doubt the bug is in the driver.
a_st: 아 노 니포 파 다코디 타푸 페세 페 후태코디 치호카
b_st: 아 노 ??? 페세 페 후태코디 치호카
a_lost: No root for driver; paraphrased as 'the function that runs the machine', which makes the clause long and could name any device-running code.
b_lost: Everything else is exact: fault for bug, the place-root locative for 'is in', the doubt root.

en: Don't touch that branch until I'm done.
a_st: 에 우 ??? 파 아 초코디 유 히 레루카마
b_st: 에 ??? 파 아 초코디 유 히 레루카마
a_lost: The condition/branch root is the if-branch in code, not a line of development; version is a snapshot, not a branch. 'Touch' was paraphrased as 'alter'.
b_lost: The code-branch root is an if-condition/branch point and would be misread; 'touch' is approximated by 'alter', losing 'do anything at all to it'.

en: Where does this function get called from?
a_st: 이 타푸 파 야 후태 호 다 추
b_st: 이 타푸 파 야 페 다 추
a_lost: 'Called' is run+function per the lexicon; the agentless clause keeps the object marker.
b_lost: 'Call' is run+function as the lexicon prescribes; the source sense of 'from' rides on the location case only, so this can also be heard as 'where is it run'.

en: The same error came back three times in a row.
a_st: 두 누 니 메루 얘타카
b_st: 우 니 메루 두 누 파 소 니유 하 메루타카
a_lost: 'In a row' (consecutively) cannot be said; 'came back' becomes a bare count of occurrences ('the same failure held three times').
b_lost: No word for consecutiveness: 'in a row' becomes 'with no gap'. 'Came back' has to reuse the repeat root that already carries 'three times', so the clause repeats itself.

en: The second run gave a lower number than the first.
a_st: 다 네 피 수포 다 나 피 수포 호 마수카
b_st: 다 네 피 수포 다 나 피 수포 호 마수카
a_lost: Restructured as a possessive comparison ('run two's number is less, from run one's number'); 'gave' is dropped since there is no comparative form.
b_lost: No comparative form, so it is restructured as 'the second run's number is less, from the first run's number'; 'gave' disappears into the possessive.

en: Are you reading the raw counts or the average?
a_st: 에 레루코디 수포 쿠 모메 파 데 추
b_st: 에 수포 쿠 모메 파 데 추
a_lost: 'Raw' is paraphrased as 'not altered'.
b_lost: No word for 'raw'; the contrast with 'average' has to carry it. No progressive aspect.

en: Put both runs on one plot.
a_st: 에 네 다 파 나 페포 페 후태카마
b_st: 에 네 다 파 나 페포 페 후태카마
a_lost: No root for plot/chart/graph; rendered as 'one display', which loses the idea of axes and of data drawn against them.
b_lost: No root for plot/chart/graph; rendered as 'one display', which loses that it is a drawn figure with axes.

en: If we heat it slower, the drift should get smaller.
a_st: 우 테해코디 파수 하 쿠태코 해 ??? 마수투키매
b_st: 우 테해코디 파수 하 쿠태코 해 ??? 테코디 쿠태코디 티페카
a_lost: No root for drift, and the language's own advice for unplanned change (increase / decrease / not-same) needs a direction the sentence does not give. Also no causative: 'we heat it' had to become 'it becomes hot', dropping the agent; 'slower' becomes plain 'slowly'.
b_lost: Also no causative: 'we heat it' has to become 'it gets hot', dropping the agent. 'Slower' has no comparative, so it is plain 'slowly'.

en: He told me the third sample was contaminated.
a_st: 우 소네 니 노코디 아 페 워야타카
b_st: 우 소네 니 노타코디 아 페 워야타카
a_lost: 'Contaminated' flattened to 'faulty': the idea that something foreign got into it is gone. No gender.
b_lost: 'Contaminated' becomes 'faulty': the listener learns the sample is no good but not that something got into it.

en: Someone left the door open; that's why the readings jumped.
a_st: 예 ??? 파 포하타카 데 무소타카
b_st: 예 ??? 파 포하타카 데 우 호 무소타카
a_lost: 'Left open' would have to be 'opened'; 'jumped' is 'increased'. The therefore-link is juxtaposition, per the grammar.
b_lost: 'Left open' becomes 'opened'; 'jumped' becomes 'increased', losing the suddenness.

en: I'm going to repeat it with a fresh batch.
a_st: 아 우 파 파캐 소네 하 메루투카마
b_st: 아 우 파 파캐 토 하 메루투카마
a_lost: 'Batch' (a quantity of material made or drawn at one time) is rendered with the sample root, which means a specimen drawn to stand for a population.
b_lost: No root for 'batch'; the sample root means a subset drawn to represent a population, which is the wrong thing, so it falls back to 'a new one'.

en: The next run will take about four hours.
a_st: 니래 다 패 캐피 소히투키매
b_st: 니래 다 패 캐피 소히투키매
a_lost: 'About/approximately' cannot be said; the predict stance carries only general uncertainty.
b_lost: No hedge for 'about'; the estimate is stated as exactly four hours, with only the predict stance softening it.

en: I don't believe that peak is real.
a_st: 아 우 무소 얘코디 시루카
b_st: 아 우 ??? 얘코디 시루카
a_lost: No root for peak; 'that rise' loses the local-maximum shape (rise then fall) that makes it a peak.
b_lost: The up/above root is spatial only and explicitly barred from amount senses, so it cannot serve.

en: Write down the room temperature every hour.
a_st: 에 이 후태 피 테해 파 새 캐피 페 미노카마
b_st: 에 나 메루 캐피 페 후태 피 테해 파 미노카마
a_lost: No root for room; 'this place's temperature' is used instead.
b_lost: No root for 'room'; rendered as 'the place's'. 'Every hour' uses the documented how-often shape, 'once per hour'.

en: How many trials do we have so far?
a_st: 야 수포 메루 이 유 히 얘 추
b_st: 아 에 하 야 수포 메루 파 이 유 히 파로타 추
a_lost: 'We have' becomes plain existence: the we-phrase ends in the with word and a case marker may not follow another marker, so 'our' cannot be formed. 'So far' is 'before now'.
b_lost: 'We have N trials' cannot be said as possession (a with-joined subject cannot take the possessor marker), so it becomes 'how many trials have we done'; 'so far' is 'before now'.

en: Nothing changed when we doubled the voltage.
a_st: 소 토 아 에 하 ??? 파 무소코디 유 페 두루타카
b_st: 소 토 두루코디 아 에 하 ??? 파 모누타코디 유 페 쿠태타카
a_lost: No electrical or physical-quantity vocabulary at all. 'Doubled' also has no expression (numerals multiply only inside numeral formation), so it was weakened to 'increased'.
b_lost: No multiplication construction, so 'doubled' degrades to 'set to a different value'. 'Nothing changed' has to be 'nothing began to be different'.

en: The clamp is loose on the left side.
a_lost: Nothing of the sentence survives: no fixture vocabulary, no tight/loose axis, and the only region roots are inside/outside, up/down, near/far.
b_lost: Nothing in this sentence is sayable: there is no left/right axis (only up, down, inside, outside, near, far), no fastener vocabulary and no tight/loose pair.

en: Hand me the small screwdriver.
a_st: 에 테 ??? 파 아 페 카푸카마
b_st: 에 테 ??? 파 아 페 카푸카마
a_lost: The frame (hand X to me, small) is fine; there is no tool vocabulary and machine will not cover it.
b_lost: The frame (hand X to me, small) is exact; only the tool is unsayable.

en: Do we have another cable like this one?
a_st: 이 하 두코디 캐토 ??? 얘 추
b_st: 이 하 두코디 ??? 얘 추
a_lost: 'Another like this one' is expressible as 'of the same kind as this'; the object itself is not. 'We have' again becomes existence.
b_lost: 'We have' also had to become bare existence, since a with-joined 'we' cannot take the possessor marker.

en: If the fan stops, shut the whole thing down.
a_st: ??? 쿠테코 해 에 투와 토 파 쿠테카마
b_st: ??? 쿠테코 해 에 투와 토 파 쿠테카마
a_lost: The conditional and 'shut the whole thing down' are exact; the fan cannot be named, and there is no causative to build 'the thing that makes it cold'.
b_lost: Everything else is exact.

en: They said the new bearings ship on Monday.
a_st: 파캐 네쿠 파 ??? 페 카푸투케
b_st: 파캐 네쿠 파 캐파 피 카유 나 페 카푸투케
a_lost: There are no weekday names and no documented convention for numbering days of a week. 'Bearings' had to be generalised to 'parts'; 'ship' is 'be sent'.
b_lost: 'Bearings' flattens to 'new parts'; no weekday names, so Monday is spelled 'the week's day one'; 'they said' survives only as the reported evidential, with no 'they'.

en: Somebody dropped this; look at the bent corner.
a_st: 예 이 파 피라 페 투도타카 에 ??? ??? 파 위카마
b_st: 예 이 파 피라 페 투도타카 에 ??? 네쿠 파 위카마
a_lost: 'Dropped' had to become 'moved it downward', losing the accident; no shape or geometry vocabulary for bent or corner.
b_lost: 'Dropped' had to become 'moved it down', which sounds deliberate; 'corner' flattens to 'part'.

en: I'll swap the pump out in the morning.
a_st: 아 ??? 파 니래 카유 페 레투카마
b_st: 아 ??? 파 니래 카유 쿠태 페 쿠피투카마 아 파캐 ??? 파 후태투카마
a_lost: Only day and night exist as parts of the cycle, so 'in the morning' was approximated to 'on the next day'. 'Swap out' weakened to 'alter'.
b_lost: No 'replace': it takes two clauses, remove then put a new one. No 'morning': 'the next day's beginning'.

en: That seal is going to leak.
a_st: 우 ??? ???투키매
b_st: 우 ??? ???투키매
a_lost: Only the pronoun and the future-predict ending survive.
b_lost: Only the stance and tense survive.

en: I'm not sure this bracket will hold.
a_st: 아 이 ??? 토시투코디 치호카
b_st: 아 이 ??? 토시투코디 치호카
a_lost: The hold root and the doubt root carry the rest well, though 'doubt' is a shade stronger than 'not sure'.
b_lost: 'Not sure' is rendered with the doubt root, which is a shade stronger than mere uncertainty.

en: Check the pressure before you open the valve.
a_st: 에 ??? 파 에 ??? 파 포하카디 히 소히카마
b_st: 에 ??? 파 에 ??? 파 포하카디 히 소히카마
a_lost: 'Check' had to be 'measure' (the check root is asking a person).
b_lost: 'Check' had to become 'measure', since the check root is asking a person whether an assumption holds.

en: Which box did the spare fittings go in?
a_st: ??? 야 ??? 페 후태 추
b_st: ??? 야 ??? 페세 페 후태 추
a_lost: Only the which-question frame and 'be located at' survive.
b_lost: Only the which-question and the inside-locative frame survive.

en: The motor runs hot after ten minutes.
a_st: 니포 푸 캐포 후 테해카
b_st: 니포 테해코디 푸 캐포 후 쿠태카
a_lost: 'Motor' generalised to machine (the root covers device or mechanism); 'runs hot' becomes 'is hot after ten minutes'.
b_lost: 'Motor' is the generic machine root; 'runs hot' becomes 'gets hot', so the link to its running is only implied.

en: We're two days behind.
a_st: 아 에 하 네 카유 노대카
b_st: 아 에 하 노대카 니유 네 카유카
a_lost: The extent 'two days' sits as a bare measure phrase before the late root, on the model of the corpus duration phrase; there is no dedicated by-how-much construction.
b_lost: There is no way to measure a degree onto a stative, so 'two days behind' has to be split into 'we are late' plus 'the gap is two days'.

en: Can you come in early tomorrow?
a_st: 에 나대 하 니래 카유 페 페세 페 투도코디 티캐 추
b_st: 에 나대 하 니래 카유 페 이 페 투도코디 티캐 추
a_lost: Asked as a literal capacity question, so the politeness of English 'can you' is lost; 'come in' is move + inside, 'tomorrow' is the next day.
b_lost: 'Come in' is 'move here'; the request is a flat ability question, with none of the politeness of 'can you'.

en: Start the long run before you leave.
a_st: 에 마소 유코디 다 파 에 페소 페 투도카디 히 쿠태카마
b_st: 에 태 다 파 에 페소 페 투도카디 히 쿠태카마
a_lost: No root for long-in-duration: it takes a relative clause 'the run that takes much time', which is heavy and can be misread as 'the run that lasts a lot' rather than naming the known long run.
b_lost: 'Long' has to be 'big' (there is no long/short of duration); 'leave' is the documented move-to-outside.

en: If the parts come Friday, we can test on Monday.
a_st: 네쿠 ??? 페 투도코 해 아 에 하 ??? 페 와코디 티캐카
b_st: 아 에 하 네쿠 파 캐파 피 카유 포 페 토소코 해 아 에 하 캐파 피 카유 나 페 와코디 티캐카
a_lost: The conditional, 'the parts come' and the ability clause are all exact; only the weekday names are unsayable.
b_lost: Both weekdays must be spelled as ordinal days of the week, which doubles the length and depends on a week-start convention the language does not fix; 'come' becomes 'we receive'.

en: She said the review moved to next week.
a_st: 우 코피 니래 캐파 페 투도타코디 워야타카
b_st: 우 코피 니래 캐파 페 투도타코디 워야타카
a_lost: No gender in the pronoun.
b_lost: 'She' is the genderless that-one.

en: He's been gone a while, so he must be at lunch.
a_st: 우 마소 유 페소 페 후태타카 우 ??? 페 후태키
b_st: 우 마소 유 헤 이 페 후태루타카 우 ??? 페 후태키
a_lost: No food, eating or meal vocabulary. 'Been gone' becomes 'was outside for much time'; the so-link is juxtaposition plus the inferred evidential.
b_lost: No food or meal vocabulary at all. 'Gone' becomes 'not located here'; 'a while' becomes 'for much time'.

en: I'll finish the wiring by Thursday.
a_st: 아 피 ??? 사세 ??? 히 초투카마
b_st: ??? 캐파 피 카유 패 히 초투카마
a_lost: 'Finish' had to be recast as 'my ...-task will be done', since the done root is stative.
b_lost: No causative for 'finish X', so it becomes 'it will be done, I commit', and the doer is only in the stance. Thursday is 'the week's day four'.

en: This is going to take longer than we told them.
a_st: 이 아 에 하 우 페 워야타코디 유 호 마소 유투키매
b_st: 아 에 하 유 파 우 페 워야타카 이 피 유 우 유 호 마소투키매
a_lost: 'Longer' is 'will take much time' with the standard in the from-phrase; no comparative form exists, so the comparison is carried by the construction only.
b_lost: A clause cannot be the standard of comparison (clause plus the from-word already means 'because'), so it splits into 'we told them a time' plus 'this one's time is more than that time'. 'Them' is 'that one'.

en: I doubt we'll be done before the holiday.
a_st: 아 아 에 하 ??? 히 초투코디 치호카
b_st: 아 아 에 하 ??? 히 초투코디 치호카
a_lost: Everything but the date-name works: doubt over a complement clause, 'be done', 'before X'.
b_lost: No calendar-event vocabulary; week, month, year and day exist but nothing names a named day off.

en: Don't put anything else on that afternoon.
a_st: 에 두루코디 사세 파 우 ??? 페 후태루카마
b_st: 에 마소 사세 파 우 카유 페 후태루카마
a_lost: Day and night are the only divisions of the cycle, and 'that day' would widen the scope. 'Anything else' became 'work that is not the same'.
b_lost: No 'afternoon', so the ban covers the whole day; 'anything else' becomes 'more tasks'.

en: What time does the shop close?
a_st: ??? 야 유 페 포해 추
b_st: ??? 야 유 페 포해 추
a_lost: No building, room or business vocabulary; the when-question and the shut root are exact.
b_lost: The place root is too generic to name a shop; the rest of the question is exact.

en: We lost half a day waiting on the order.
a_st: 아 에 하 체 파 카유 피 네쿠 수초타카
b_st: 아 에 하 ??? 파 수초타카 우 니유 ??? 카유카
a_lost: No fractions, so 'half a day' is 'a part of a day'; 'lost' (wasted) is carried only by the blocked-on root; 'the order' is the ask-for-action root, which is a request, not a purchase order.
b_lost: There are no fractions (only integer numerals), the list/order root is sequence and would be a false friend, and time cannot be 'lost' - the best that remains is 'we were blocked by ???; that gap was ??? day'.

en: I don't think that's the real cause.
a_st: 아 우 얘 대코디 시루카
b_st: 아 우 얘 대코디 시루카
a_lost: 'I don't think' is 'I do not believe'; 'real' is the true root used attributively.
b_lost: 'Think' is the believe side of the knowing carve; 'real' is 'true'.

en: Why do you want to do it that way?
a_st: 에 우 파 우 하 파로코디 야 헤 티파 추
b_st: 에 우 파 우 하 파로코디 야 헤 티파 추
a_lost: 'That way' is the manner with-phrase over the far pronoun, matching the how-question in the corpus.
b_lost: 'That way' is the documented manner with-phrase.

en: Let's do the simple version first.
a_st: 아 에 하 타로 파테 파 파로투카메
b_st: 아 에 하 타로 파테 파 리투카마
a_lost: No hortative: 'let's' is we + future + the propose stance. 'First' is unexpressed, as in the corpus. 'Simple' is the easy root.
b_lost: No hortative: 'let's' is a we-subject with the intend stance. 'First' goes unsaid, as the corpus itself does. 'Simple' is 'easy'.

en: If you're right, then the whole model is wrong.
a_st: 에 얘하코 해 투와 헤도 얘루카
b_st: 에 얘하코 해 투와 ??? 얘루카
a_lost: No root for model (a worked-out account of how something behaves); 'the whole explanation' is the nearest honest thing and loses the predictive, structured sense.
b_lost: Pattern, plan and definition all mean something else; nothing names a theoretical model. 'Wrong' of a model has to be 'not true'.

en: He says we should start over.
a_st: 우 아 에 하 메루코디 티페코디 워야카
b_st: 우 아 에 하 메루코디 티페코디 워야카
a_lost: 'Start over' is the repeat root (do the whole thing again from the beginning). Two stacked subordinators make it heavy. No gender.
b_lost: 'Start over' is the repeat root, which is exactly 'do the whole thing again from the beginning'. 'He' is genderless.

en: You've already decided, haven't you?
a_st: 아 에 초해타코디 치카
b_st: 아 에 초해타코디 치카
a_lost: The tag is rendered as an explicit check-an-assumption clause ('I check that you decided'); 'already' is unexpressed, as in the corpus.
b_lost: No word for 'already'; the tag has to become an explicit 'I check that...', which is more formal than the English.

en: I'd rather fix it now than ship it broken.
a_st: 아 우 파 이 유 페 라코디 티파카 아 우 파 우 노코디 유 페 카푸코디 티파루카
b_st: 아 우 파 이 유 페 라코디 티파카 아 노코디 토 파 카푸코디 티파루카
a_lost: No preference construction ('rather X than Y'): it splits into want-this / not-want-that, which loses the ranking and doubles the length.
b_lost: No preference construction: 'rather X than Y' splits into 'I want X' plus 'I do not want Y', which loses the ranking. 'Ship' is the generic send root.

en: That won't work with the old hardware.
a_st: 우 파캐루코디 니포 하 로루투키매
b_st: 우 파캐루코디 니포 하 로루투키매
a_lost: 'Work' is 'be good (for its purpose)'; 'hardware' is machine; 'old' is 'not new'.
b_lost: 'Hardware' is the generic machine root; 'work' is the good root ('be good for its purpose').

en: I'm not convinced either way yet.
a_st: 아 이 파 시루카 아 우 파 시루카
b_st: 아 이 파 시루카 아 우 파 시루카
a_lost: The lexicon notes that one can neither believe nor doubt but coins no root for suspended judgement, so it becomes two flat denials of belief; 'either way' and 'yet' are lost.
b_lost: No 'either way' and no 'yet': the only honest rendering is two flat clauses, 'I do not believe this; I do not believe that', which sounds more settled than the English.

en: Pick one and we'll move on.
a_st: 에 나 토 파 야헤카마 아 에 하 쿠로투카마
b_st: 에 나 토 파 야헤카마 아 에 하 쿠로투카마
a_lost: 'Move on' is the continue root; 'and' is juxtaposition, as the grammar requires.
b_lost: 'And' is juxtaposition, as the grammar requires.

en: We agreed last week to keep the old format.
a_st: 아 에 하 파캐루코디 캐토 파 모나코디 니로 캐파 페 두하타카
b_st: 아 에 하 파캐루코디 왜 캐토 파 모나코디 니로 캐파 페 두하타카
a_lost: 'Format' is the kind/type root; 'keep' is the hold-fixed root; 'old' is 'not new'.
b_lost: 'Format' is the compound 'file kind'; 'keep' is the hold-fixed root.

en: Fine, we'll try yours first.
a_st: 아 두하카 아 에 하 에 피 토 파 와투카마
b_st: 아 두하카 아 에 하 에 피 토 파 와투카마
a_lost: 'Fine' becomes 'I agree'; 'yours' needs a noun after the possessor, so it is 'your thing'; 'first' is unexpressed.
b_lost: 'Fine' becomes a plain 'I agree', losing the grudging note; 'first' goes unsaid; 'yours' has to be 'your thing'.
